nodes.name: Ni foam cleaning
nodes.procedure: A piece of Ni foam (NF 2×2 cm) was soaked in HCl solution (6 M) for 15 min and washed with deionized water and absolute ethanol for two times.

nodes.name: NiFe2O4/NiFe LDH solvothermal synthesis (1:1.5)
nodes.procedure: Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (0.5 mmol), 0.75 mmol of FeCl2·4H2O, and 1.5 mmol of NaHCO3 were dissolved in the solvents of 20 mL of deionized water and 15 mL of methanol by agitation for 0.5 h. Afterward, the solution was shifted to a 40 mL stainless steel autoclave with a Teflon liner and inserted cleaned Ni foam. Then, the autoclave was maintained at 120°C for 2 h. After the reaction, the product covered on Ni foam was washed with deionized water and absolute ethanol for three times and vacuum-dried at 50°C for 6 h.

nodes.procedure: The precursor nanosheet array was first prepared with 0.5 mmol of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 1 mmol of FeCl2·4H2O while other parameters were kept constant as that of NiFe LDH nanosheet array. nodes.source_text: The electrochemical measurements were performed on a CHI 760e electrochemical workstation... with a three-electrode experimental setup at 25°C in 1.0 M KOH electrolyte. The working electrode was the NiFe₂O₄/NiFe LDH/NF... loading mass was 2.8 mg cm⁻²... Platinum wire... Ag/AgCl... LSV was performed at 5 mV s⁻¹ with 90% iR-correction... overpotential of 213 mV at 100 mA cm⁻²... 500 mA cm⁻² at 242 mV and 1000 mA cm⁻² at 265 mV... Tafel slope of 28.2 mV dec⁻¹... Faradaic efficiency of over 92.6%... current densities at overpotentials of 202, 230, and 242 mV all retain over 97% during the 20 h... C_dl of NiFe₂O₄/NiFe LDH was 11.9 mF cm⁻²... R_ct of NiFe₂O₄/NiFe LDH was 0.34 Ω.

The HER activity... overpotential of 101 mV to drive 10 mA cm⁻² and 229 mV for 100 mA cm⁻²... 500 mA cm⁻² at 297 mV and 750 mA cm⁻² at 314 mV... Tafel plot... 67.1 mV dec⁻¹... 20 h constant overpotential electrolysis at 150, 259, and 298 mV... current densities were all only slightly dropped.

nodes.description: Overall water splitting (OWS) in two-electrode configuration
nodes.source_text: Overall water splitting tests using NiFe₂O₄/NiFe LDH/NF as both the anode and the cathode were performed in a two-electrode configuration through a LSV polarization curve at 5 mV s⁻¹ (with 90% iR-correction)... current density of 10 mA cm⁻² at 1.535 V... 500 mA cm⁻² at 1.932 V... 20 h chronoamperometric tests at 1.60, 1.82, and 1.94 V all showed only a slight degradation... current densities were all remained over 94.4% for exceeding 40 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe₂O₄/NiFe LDH shows mixed phases of cubic NiFe₂O₄ (JCPDS no. 74-2081) with peaks at 18.4°, 30.3°, 35.7°, 43.4°, 53.8°, 57.4°, 63.0°, 74.5° and NiFe LDH (α-phase Ni(OH)₂, JCPDS no. 38-0715) with peaks at 11.3°, 22.7°, 33.5°, 34.4°, 38.8°, 46.0°, 60.0°, 61.2°.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1 shows the product is the mixed phases of NiFe₂O₄ and NiFe LDH when the raw material ratio of Ni/Fe was 1:1.5...

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe₂O₄/NiFe LDH shows bands at 211, 275, 458, 533, and 683 cm⁻¹ indicating coexistence of NiFe₂O₄ and NiFe LDH phases. Pure NiFe₂O₄ shows peaks at 211, 275, 683 cm⁻¹; pure NiFe LDH at 455, 525, 703 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As for NiFe₂O₄/NiFe LDH product, the bands at 211, 275, 458, 533, and 683 cm⁻¹ indicate that the NiFe₂O₄ and NiFe LDH phases coexist.

nodes.characterization_summary: FESEM images show NiFe₂O₄/NiFe LDH nanosheet array structure ca. 1.5 μm lateral size with uniform ~100 nm diameter nanoparticles attached on nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The field emission SEM (FESEM) images of the NiFe₂O₄/NiFe LDH in Figure 3a,b showed that the product was a nanosheet array structure, with uniform nanoparticles attached on the nanosheets, where the nanosheets were ca. 1.5 μm in lateral size and the nanoparticles were about 100 nm in diameter.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM image confirms ~100 nm nanoparticles attached on NiFe₂O₄/NiFe LDH nanosheets; elemental mapping shows uniform Ni, Fe, O distribution across nanosheet with higher Fe/O in nanoparticle domains.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3c presented the STEM image on NiFe₂O₄/NiFe LDH, from which the nanoparticles with a size of about 100 nm attached on the nanosheets can be clearly identified.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows adjacent fringes of 0.30 nm (220) planes of NiFe₂O₄ and 0.27 nm (101) planes of NiFe LDH in NiFe₂O₄/NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image of the NiFe₂O₄/NiFe LDH in Figure 3d revealed that the adjacent fringes were 0.30 and 0.27 nm respectively...

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe₂O₄/NiFe LDH shows Ni 2p peaks at 855.5, 873.3 eV (Ni²⁺), 856.5, 874.3 eV (Ni³⁺); Fe 2p pre-peak 706.4 eV, 711.8, 724.7 eV (Fe³⁺), 709.4, 723.1 eV (Fe²⁺); O 1s at 529.9 eV (oxides), 531.5 eV (hydroxides), 533.3 eV (adsorbed water).
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS was applied to analyze the valence states of Ni and Fe in NiFe₂O₄/NiFe LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX results show atomic ratio of Ni and Fe in three products basically in accordance with raw material ratio.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDX results of three products in Figure S4 revealed that the atomic ratio of Ni and Fe is basically in accordance with the raw material ratio...

nodes.characterization_summary: C_dl of NiFe₂O₄/NiFe LDH is 11.9 mF cm⁻², higher than NiFe LDH (7.7 mF cm⁻²) and NiFe₂O₄ (6.6 mF cm⁻²).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The C_dl of NiFe₂O₄/NiFe LDH was 11.9 mF cm⁻², while that of NiFe LDH and NiFe₂O₄ was 7.7 and 6.6 mF cm⁻², respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe₂O₄/NiFe LDH shows smallest R_ct of 0.34 Ω, compared to NiFe LDH (1.90 Ω) and NiFe₂O₄ (1.00 Ω); largest low-frequency slope indicating best mass transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The fitting results of the semicircles in Figure S16 reveal that the R_ct of NiFe₂O₄/NiFe LDH was 0.34 Ω...
When the raw material ratio of Ni/Fe was kept 1:1.5 in 5 mL of deionized water and 30 mL of methanol, the product primarily showed the reflections of NiFe LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pure NiFe₂O₄ shows diffraction peaks at 18.4°, 30.3°, 35.7°, 43.4°, 53.8°, 57.4°, 63.0°, 74.5° attributed to (111), (220), (311), (400), (422), (511), (440), (533) planes of cubic NiFe₂O₄ (JCPDS no. 74-2081).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As the raw material ratio of Ni/Fe was raised to 1:2 in 5 mL of deionized water and 30 mL of methanol, only the NiFe₂O₄ phase was presented after calcination.
